title: SenProjectDocumentation
purpose: This document consolidates the requirements expressed while designing, building, testing and operating sensayantan.github.io — a static personal site with a browser-based CMS, an automated daily news brief, and a retrieval search over autism research. It converts the request history into epics, user stories, acceptance criteria and assumptions.
vision: As the site owner, I want a personal site I can publish to from a browser, that carries an automated daily brief and a research search I can defend, so that everything I put my name to is current, honest about its limits, and maintainable without a build step.
principles: Measure, do not eyeball. Layout and relevance decisions are settled by measuring the rendered page or scoring real queries, never by reading the code and assuming.
A fix belongs where it survives. Generated files are overwritten, so changes go into the script that re-applies them, not into the output.
Honest about limits. Search results are presented as a similarity search over literature, never as health information.
No silent failure. A stale cache, a blocked pop-up and an invalid config each announce themselves rather than looking like nothing happened.
Cite or do not claim. Every factual sentence in a generated answer carries a citation, and citations never outnumber the sources retrieved.
No build step. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no bundler or framework, so the site stays editable years from now.
Secrets never enter the repository. Tokens live as platform secrets; only values that are public by design are committed.
Trade-offs are recorded. Where a choice departs from convention, the reasoning is written into the code so it is not silently reverted.

epics.title: Autism research search
epics.summary: A question-answering search over real autism literature, built to show its working rather than to sound authoritative.

stories.title: Real corpus from public sources
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want the index built from real published abstracts and trial records so that answers trace to actual research rather than to a model's recollection.
acceptance_criteria: PubMed abstracts are retrieved via E-utilities, esearch followed by efetch.
ClinicalTrials.gov records are retrieved via the v2 JSON API with cursor paging.
Roughly 1,500 abstracts and 400 trial records are fetched.
Parsers handle structured abstracts, inline markup, MedlineDate values and collective authors.
Parser tests run from fixtures and require no network access.
assumptions: Both APIs remain free and require no key.
An NCBI API key raises the rate limit but is never required.
Credentials are read from the environment and never committed.

stories.title: Search by meaning, not keywords
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want a question to find papers that answer it rather than papers that repeat its words.
acceptance_criteria: Dense embeddings use BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, 384 dimensions, 512-token window.
The query instruction prefix is stored inside the index so query and document settings cannot drift apart.
Ranking is cosine similarity over unit-normalised vectors, brute force top-k.
assumptions: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 was rejected because its 256 word-piece window truncates abstracts.
At roughly 1,900 documents a vector database would cost more than it saves.

stories.title: A relevance threshold set by measurement
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want the cut-off between a real match and noise derived from measurement so that it can be defended and re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: A calibration script measures the off-topic ceiling against the on-topic floor.
It refuses to suggest a threshold when those two ranges overlap.
Calibration uses six unrelated control questions rather than one.
The threshold was recalibrated to 0.56 after a genuine result cleared the previous floor by 0.002.
assumptions: A single off-topic probe measures the wrong thing; a bicycle question scored 0.514 against a cycling trial.

stories.title: Free-text questions with a written answer
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want to ask my own question and receive a written summary, not only a list of links.
acceptance_criteria: A Cloudflare Worker performs retrieval and generation within the free tier.
The index ships as a flat vectors file and a documents file, with no database.
The Worker refuses to run when the index's model name does not match its own.
Retrieval failure is fatal; generation failure still returns ranked results.
Every factual sentence carries a citation, and citation markers never exceed the number of sources.
assumptions: The Workers AI free tier allows 10,000 neurons per day.
The "@cf/" prefix marks first-party models, not free-tier ones.
Third-party models require a provider key and billing and are therefore out of scope.

stories.title: Presented honestly
stories.narrative: As a parent arriving at this page, I want to understand immediately what it is and is not, so that I do not mistake a similarity search for medical advice.
acceptance_criteria: A prominent banner states that this is a research search tool, not health information.
The page carries a noindex directive.
Outbound result links are restricted to pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and clinicaltrials.gov.
Prepared and free-text questions share one pipeline and one presentation.
Sources collapse into a quieter block so that the summary leads.
assumptions: A reader here may be a worried parent rather than a researcher.

stories.title: Correct the corpus imbalance
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want trial records to surface in proportion to their share of the corpus so that ongoing research is not under-represented.
acceptance_criteria: Trial records appear roughly in proportion to their 21% share of the corpus.
assumptions: Trials are 21% of the corpus but produce about 9% of results, because protocol language sits further from how people phrase questions.

stories.title: Prevalence figures with citations
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want current prevalence figures alongside the search so that the scale of the subject is clear.
acceptance_criteria: Each figure carries a named source and a date.
assumptions: No API exists, so the figures are hand-curated and need re-checking when the source updates.

epics.title: Daybreak daily news brief
epics.summary: A daily brief generated outside this repository, made to behave like part of this site once it lands.

stories.title: Site conventions survive a new edition
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want this site's conventions re-applied automatically so that they stop disappearing every morning.
acceptance_criteria: A patch script re-applies conventions on every push touching the editions folder.
Each step checks its own marker, so running the script twice changes nothing.
Steps anchor on markup the script itself controls rather than on generator output.
Behaviour is verified against a genuinely new edition, not only existing ones.
assumptions: The generator's structure drifts between versions.
Editions never load the site stylesheet; they are a separate design system with inline CSS.

stories.title: Reach older editions
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want to open any past edition by date so that the archive is not write-only.
acceptance_criteria: A calendar page lists every edition that exists.
Days with no edition are greyed out and cannot be selected.
The index is generated from the files present, not from a weekday rule.
Month paging is clamped to the range that has editions.
Dates are parsed field by field rather than with a UTC-parsing date constructor.
assumptions: Daybreak skips Sundays but has also missed ordinary weekdays, so a weekday rule would offer days that 404.
A UTC-parsed date renders a day early anywhere west of Greenwich.

stories.title: Open the archive without losing the edition
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want the archive to open beside what I am reading rather than replacing it.
acceptance_criteria: The archive opens in a separate sized window.
A chrome-off parameter strips site header and footer, and carries through to the edition opened from it.
A blocked pop-up shows a notice with a plain-link fallback.
The link still opens a new tab with JavaScript disabled.
assumptions: Pop-up blockers are silent; window.open simply returns null.
Mobile browsers ignore the requested size and open a tab instead.

stories.title: One consistent header and a usable section menu
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want the header to stay put as I move between pages, and the section menu to stay reachable as I scroll.
acceptance_criteria: Header height, background, brand position, nav span and active pill are identical across all four pages at desktop width.
The category bar occupies one row at every width from 390px to 1440px.
The bar sticks while scrolling, positioned below the site header rather than underneath it.
Section anchors are offset so a jump does not land beneath the pinned bar.
assumptions: Eleven full section titles cannot fit one row at any readable size, so the bar carries short labels and the headings keep the full names.
The generator's own site header is already sticky at the top, so the category bar must measure it rather than assume a height.
stories.notes: At 390px the Daybreak header is 75px against 63px elsewhere. The site collapses to a hamburger at that width and an edition has none to collapse into; matching exactly requires injecting one.

stories.title: Restore a lower bound on edition contents
stories.narrative: As the report owner, I want an edition with no verified stories to be refused rather than published empty.
acceptance_criteria: A research run that verifies nothing refuses the edition.
assumptions: Per-section minimums should stay soft; only the overall floor should be hard.
The original floor of five stories was replaced by per-section minimums, which were then relaxed, leaving no floor at all.

stories.title: Stop discarding promoted stories
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want a grave regional story to appear somewhere rather than vanish because the lead section was full.
acceptance_criteria: A promoted story that cannot fit Top News stays in its origin section.
assumptions: Confirmed by simulation — twelve grave Africa candidates produce ten Top News entries, zero Africa entries and two discarded.

epics.title: Blog authoring and publishing
epics.summary: Write posts in a browser and have them appear, without touching the repository.

stories.title: Publish from the browser
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want to write and publish a post from a browser so that publishing does not require a local checkout.
acceptance_criteria: The admin commits Markdown straight to the default branch.
GitHub sign-in runs through a Cloudflare Worker OAuth proxy.
The token is delivered to an explicit origin, never to a wildcard.
A workflow renders posts and listing data on every content change.
assumptions: The OAuth client id is public by design; the secret exists only as a platform secret.

stories.title: Banner, listing and comments
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want posts to look like articles, with a picture and a way to respond.
acceptance_criteria: A banner image renders above the article and as the listing thumbnail.
Posts are listed one per row.
A video URL embeds as a player, with the id extracted rather than the input interpolated into the frame source.
Comments are backed by GitHub Discussions.
assumptions: A video link pasted into the attachment field produced a broken relative URL, so the fields are now distinct.

stories.title: Publishing that actually publishes
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want a published post to appear and a deleted post to disappear.
acceptance_criteria: Listing data is fetched with cache disabled, so a CDN cannot serve a stale listing.
Deleting a post removes both its listing entry and its rendered page.
Imported posts that have no markdown source survive a rebuild.
assumptions: Entries written by the renderer are marked, and only marked entries are retired when their source disappears.

stories.title: An editor that matches how a post is written
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want the form to ask for what a post actually needs and nothing more.
acceptance_criteria: The date field has no clock.
An optional end date produces a date range in the listing.
Tags accept a comma-separated line.
Images can be placed inline within the body.
assumptions: The CMS cannot multi-select uploads, resize images in the editor, or drag-reorder them; those remain unavailable.

stories.title: Uploads that do not overwrite each other
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want a new upload never to replace an existing image silently.
acceptance_criteria: Each post uploads into its own folder.
Existing images are migrated so every post's picker finds its own files.
Media paths are root-absolute so the admin resolves previews correctly.
assumptions: The CMS does not uniquify uploads; a repeated filename replaces the file at that path.
Two files of the same name within the same post still collide.

epics.title: Reading experience
epics.summary: Layout and typography decisions, each settled by measurement.

stories.title: Use the available width
stories.narrative: As a reader on a wide screen, I want the page to use the space rather than sit in a narrow strip.
acceptance_criteria: The blog post page is 1180px with a 1000px text column.
The experiment page fills its shell, presenting one width down the page.
There is no horizontal overflow from 390px to 1600px.
assumptions: Long lines were chosen deliberately over empty space; the blog body runs about 135 characters per line and the experiment page about 170, against the 75 usually recommended.
The reasoning is recorded in the stylesheet so it is not reverted as an oversight.

stories.title: Chrome never covers content
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want the fixed footer to stay clear of the last thing on the page.
acceptance_criteria: Body padding clears the fixed footer at every width.
Clearance is measured at the true page bottom rather than mid-scroll.
assumptions: The footer stacks to three rows on a phone and is taller than it appears.

epics.title: Pipeline and safeguards
epics.summary: The checks that exist because something shipped broken and nobody noticed until it was in front of a person.

stories.title: Never serve a stale stylesheet or script
stories.narrative: As a reader, I want the page I load to use the code that was actually deployed.
acceptance_criteria: CSS and JavaScript share one version counter and are bumped together.
A check script fails on any reference that carries no version at all.
assumptions: A stale script is worse than a stale stylesheet; it makes a feature silently absent rather than merely ugly.

stories.title: Catch a broken CMS config before a person does
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want an invalid admin configuration to fail in CI rather than to take the admin down.
acceptance_criteria: A validator checks markdown buttons, editor components, widget names and datetime fields against their allowed values.
It fails on the exact value that previously broke the admin, not merely passing on a corrected file.
The workflow runs it, and the admin folder is in the workflow's trigger paths.
assumptions: Parsing as YAML is not the same as being schema-valid, and only the CMS knows the schema.
An invalid value replaces the entire admin with an error rather than degrading.

stories.title: A pipeline that can be run on demand
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want to run the render pipeline without waiting for a content change.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow can be dispatched manually.
assumptions: The push trigger watches content paths, so a change to the workflow itself could not exercise it.

stories.title: Document the work as a backlog
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want the request history expressed as epics and stories so that the reasoning behind the site is legible later.
acceptance_criteria: Epics, stories, acceptance criteria and assumptions render as a backlog.
Content lives in one file that both the admin and an external agent can edit.
The page is unlisted and carries a noindex directive.
assumptions: Written after the fact from the request history, so statuses describe what shipped rather than what was planned.

stories.title: Merge in the Daybreak epics
stories.narrative: As the site owner, I want the Daybreak epics on the same page so that one backlog covers the whole site.
acceptance_criteria: Daybreak epics appear alongside these, grouped separately, without reformatting either set.
assumptions: The page groups epics by their project field, so neither set needs renumbering.

definition_of_done: The change is measured or tested, not assumed to work from reading the code.
Generated output is produced by a script, never hand-edited.
Asset versions are bumped and the consistency check passes.
Both workflows are green and the render step commits nothing unexpected.
Any trade-off that departs from convention is written into the code.
out_of_scope: Multi-select uploads, in-editor image resizing and drag-reordering — the CMS does not support them.
Paid APIs and third-party hosted models requiring provider billing.
A build step, bundler or front-end framework.
Presenting search results as health information of any kind.
